statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Current Tail risk remains in the low band.
recommendation: Current evidence supports low Tail risk while technology-sector and event stress remain elevated; the U.S. cash open and 10:00 ET data window are the nearest defined checkpoints.
headline: Low Tail risk as Nasdaq-100 futures stabilize before European liquidity
body: Monday's Nasdaq decline was technology- and semiconductor-led, but fresh pre-Europe evidence shows Nasdaq-100 futures modestly positive rather than extending one-way. Oil is below Monday's higher levels, reducing cross-asset alignment. Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales at 10:00 ET are the nearest volatility checkpoint.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail moved from low into WATCH during Monday's technology-led selloff, briefly reached elevated in the 18:00-19:00 UTC hours, then eased through WATCH and returned to low after midnight. Stress was extreme through much of Monday before falling to elevated overnight.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours remain event-sensitive but do not imply a one-way path. Tail is projected to stay low through Europe, rise into WATCH around the U.S. cash open and 10:00 ET Consumer Confidence/New Home Sales window, and ease if post-release trade is two-way. Wednesday's GDP/PCE/durable-goods and Nvidia catalysts remain the next major risk cluster.
